title: Tiwala 14 soybean (NSIC Sy 12): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Tiwala 14 soybean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Tiwala 14 soybean is a grain soybean variety. About 83 days to harvest, 2 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Tiwala 14 soybean is a grain soybean variety, also sold or known as NSIC Sy 12. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2019 as NSIC 2019 Sy 12. It takes about 83 days from sowing to harvest, with 2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Sy 12, this is the same soybean. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [soybean variety finder](/crop-varieties/soybean), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 83 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in the wet season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Tiwala 14 soybean takes about 83 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 19 grain soybean varieties with a day count, 84.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 2 t/ha matches the average of its group, 1.92. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 83 to 92 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit soybean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 13.1 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is yellow.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 1.97 t/ha dry season, 2.59 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** Yellow seed, about 11 to 13 g per 100 seeds.
**Where:** Negros Occidental and Bukidnon, mainly wet season.
Resistant to rust and bacterial pustule.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of IPB's 2019 Tiwala releases for Negros Occidental and Bukidnon, also tried as edamame in Ilocos. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Tiwala 14 soybean

It is recommended for the wet season. Grain soybean goes to feed and food processors, while vegetable soybean, or edamame, is picked green. Pick a variety rated against rust, the main soybean disease here.

items.q: Is NSIC Sy 12 the same as Tiwala 14?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Sy 12 is another name for Tiwala 14, registered as NSIC 2019 Sy 12. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 83 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Tiwala 14?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
